reason: The text depicts Moses and Aaron, the Hebrew leaders, consistently working to liberate the Hebrew people from Egyptian slavery. Moses repeatedly confronts Pharaoh, demanding 'שַׁלַּח אֶת־ עַמִּי' (Let my people go), performs miraculous signs to convince him, and provides detailed protective instructions to the Hebrew elders and people for the Passover. At no point do the Hebrew leaders show antagonism toward their own people. The only antagonism toward the Hebrews depicted in the text is from Pharaoh, the Egyptian ruler, who refuses to release them despite the plagues.
